newsitem.title: USA: One dead, two missing in fireworks blast in U.S.
newsitem.headline: One dead, two missing in fireworks blast in U.S.

text.p: One man was killed and two others were missing on Friday after a barge loaded with fireworks exploded during a Fourth of July celebration along the Mississippi River near St. Louis on Thursday night.
"It was an accident," said Alton Assistant Fire Chief Tim Spaulding in a telephone interview. He said one of the fireworks misfired and collided with another, sparking the explosion.
Fireworks displays are traditionally used in the United States to celebrate Independence Day on July 4.
Search efforts continued for the two missing men, who were presumed to have drowned. Their identities were being withheld pending notification of relatives.
"If they went into the water without life vests in the middle of the night and possibly unconscious, everything looks pretty bad for them," said Spaulding.

All three men were employees of The Mad Bomber pyrotechnics company of Kingsbury, Indiana. Two other employees were also aboard the barge. Rafaeil Gonzales, 32, suffered a sprained ankle and Carlos Alicia was unharmed. Spaulding said all five employees were in their mid-30s and from the Chcago area.
Spectators were not in danger of injury from the explosion, as the barge was anchored in the middle of the river and another barge was connected to it to create a protective barrier.
Spaulding said a tugboat linked to the barges pushed them upriver to allow the fire department to douse the flames.
